h1: Android app development, from idea to Google Play
overview: We design and build a native Android app in Kotlin with Jetpack Compose. We agree the screens and features in writing, build in short steps and test on several phone sizes and Android versions. You install each build from a Play internal testing link, and when you are happy we prepare the release in your own Google Play Console. You receive the full source code at handover.

faq: Do I need my own Google Play developer account?
Yes, so you own the app and its listing. Google charges a one-time registration fee. We guide you through setup and ask you to add us as a user with limited permissions, never to share your password.

Google decides. We build to Google Play policies and prepare the listing, the Data safety form and the testing track. Some newer developer accounts must run a closed test with testers first, and we explain the current rules.
You do. At handover you get the full Android Studio project, the Gradle files and notes on how to build a release bundle. Open-source libraries keep their own licences, which we list for you.
Which Android versions do you support?
We agree a minimum version with you, usually one that covers the large majority of active devices. Supporting very old versions adds testing time, so we suggest a sensible cut-off.
